comments.author: @iyex-ho5um
comments.text:
I’m from Kiribati, by the way. Why the heck do you outsiders keep telling us that we’re going to sink or that the ocean is going to take our homes? You’ve been telling us that for over 50 years, yet the islands are still there—not even an inch has changed. We’ve never said it’s sinking because we’re still living here without any difficulties recently.

Climate change is nothing but delusional. You guys should keep your own theories, but don’t just call us “sinking.” Your theory only started in the 1960s. You need to learn more about the world—you haven’t discovered everything yet.   The ocean is still only about 5% discovered, and you can’t even predict when an earthquake or cyclone is going to happen. So how the hell can you predict sea-level rise? There’s still so much more to learn.

replies.author: @ThePlanetJournalGlobe
replies.text: We truly appreciate your perspective as a resident, @iyex-ho5um. Our goal was to highlight the strength of your community, and we hear your frustration with how the outside media often portrays your home.

comments.author: @Teefam93
comments.text: I recalled when a friend of mine from Australia was in Kiribati under a catholic school exchange program, he asked, there's so little here in Kiribati, why are you guys so happy everyday?  At first I didn't understand the question because I've never lived in their world. Now that I've seen how different life in each countrys, I finally understood the question. The answer would be, smaller pacific states have little to nothing to lose, so we are always grateful for what little we have. It's nothing big, but it's home.
